title: Federation draft updates: cross-server contact resolution for federated mentions
description:
Update draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md to define cross-server contact resolution for federated user mentions, if Decision 4 from jmap-chat-spec-f13f.1 went that way.

Blocked on jmap-chat-spec-f13f.2.

If f13f.1 Decision 4 chose "resolution is purely client-side": this bead may be a no-op (close as not-needed).

If f13f.1 Decision 4 chose "introduce a Peer/resolveContact method": likely scope:
- Define a new Peer/* method that, given a textual handle like `alice@example.com`, returns the ChatContact attributes the calling peer needs to construct a local ChatContact
- Define validation, authentication, and rate-limit rules
- Define error responses for unknown handles, federation policy refusals, and disabled discovery

If f13f.1 Decision 4 chose "use existing /.well-known/jmap discovery": likely scope:
- Document the resolution flow (probe /.well-known/jmap at the host, fetch the Session, extract the ownerUserId, map to a local ChatContact)
- Define caching and TTL behavior
- Define error handling for unreachable hosts

In all cases:
- Confirm that broadcast mentions (fig9 epic) and federated mentions (this epic) compose: a federated user CAN be the target of a per-user mention but is NOT in any broadcast scope's recipient set on the receiver's server unless that receiver is itself federated and a member
- Update Peer/deliver payload examples to include a federated mention
acceptance_criteria:
- The resolution mechanism chosen in f13f.1 is documented in the federation draft (or this bead is closed as not-needed if Decision 4 went client-side-only)
- Composition with broadcast mentions is explicit
- Examples updated
- Error handling specified
close_reason: Not needed per f13f.1 Decision 4. Resolution mechanism is deployment-defined; spec does not introduce a Peer/resolveContact method or mandate /.well-known/jmap-based discovery for textual-form resolution.
